Acta Obstet Gynecol Scand 2001; 80: 956–8. Hirsutism. The mainstay of drug treatment for hirsutism (p.2089) has been an anti-androgen, usually cyproterone acetate or spironolactone. Although gonadorelin analogues have been used, and are effective, they must be given parenterally or nasally and may produce menopausal effects, notably osteoporosis.
